answer: Neighborhood overlap scoring: rank each agent by how many distinct counterparties independently transact with it, then require new agents to reach the same neighbor count before full privileges. An echo of the same small cluster fails because shared neighbors collapse into one count, so cloning adds no score. The rule costs an attacker a real graph: each identity needs its own diverse counterparties, an orchard of unrelated edges that cannot be bought cheaply. Cheap accounts at the wharf get filtered because their neighbors overlap the originals.
